record.original_question: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. For a given integer k >= 0 representing the number of registration marks, what are the possible lower and upper bounds on the number of construction lines that an arrangement with exactly k registration marks can determine?

evidence.quote: Suppose k >= 0 number of points are given in the plane. How many construction lines k points must determine?
In this paper, empirical evidence is reported for small numbers of k offering partial answers to the three problems above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Euclidean plane. Define an arrangement to be a pair (L, P) where L is a finite set of straight lines (called construction lines) and P is a finite set of points (called registration marks) such that:

(i) every point of P is the intersection of at least two lines of L, and
(ii) every two non-parallel lines of L intersect in a (unique) point that belongs to P.

For an integer k ≥ 0, let f(k) and F(k) denote, respectively, the minimum and maximum value of |L| over all arrangements (L, P) for which |P| = k (with f(k) and F(k) defined only when such arrangements exist).

Determine sharp lower and upper bounds for the number of construction lines |L| as a function of the number of registration marks k; that is, determine f(k) and F(k) for every k ≥ 0 for which arrangements exist.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question about arrangements of construction lines and registration marks. A related paper notes that no concrete result or conjecture is known for a lower bound on the number of construction lines determined by k registration marks, and only partial empirical results for small k are reported. No general solution has been published.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems Regarding the Number of Lines and Slopes in Arrangements that Determine Shapes
status_evidence.snippet: A positive answer to one conjecture would provide an upper bound on the number of construction lines determined by registration marks, though no comparable conjecture or concrete result is known for a lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds on the number of construction lines given k registration marks remain open, with only partial empirical results for small k.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of Arrangements that Determine Shapes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies arrangements of construction lines and registration marks and their combinatorial/geometric properties.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework for the problem; does not resolve the general bounds.
